newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Edgars sees tough retail market into 1997.
newsitem.headline: Edgars sees tough retail market into 1997.

text.p: South African stores group Edgars Stores Ltd, reporting disappointing first-half results on Tuesday, said it expected tough trading conditions to continue through at least the first half of 1997.
"There is little prospect of lower interest rates in the short term and retail markets are unlikely to regain momentum before the middle of calendar 1997," the group said in a statement.
Against this backdrop, the group would continue to trade aggressively and "make every effort to match last year's record earnings for the full year to March".

Attributable income fell five percent in the six months to end-September at 145.1 million rand and the company said retail sales of 2,659.9 million rand versus 2,318.9 million a year earlier were below expectations.
However, weak sales growth was in some measure a consequence of the success of new extended credit products launch last year, it said.
"In the main, customers have managed these accounts responsibly and, in endeavouring to reduce outstanding balances, have restricted their pruchases this year," Edgars said.
The company's flagship Edgars shops remained the engine of the business, with new retail developments continuing to drive divisional earnings growth of seven percent to 131.0 million rand.

Sales House managed earnings growth of only three percent to 25.2 million while Jet sank into a loss of 12.1 million from a profit of 3.4 million and Shoecorp losses widened to 7.2 million from 4.0 million.
The Zimbabwe division, consolidated for the first time, boosted earnings to 6.4 million rand from 3.5 million as it continued to increase market share.
